entries.label: Cimenterie — ciment au premier plan
entries.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: Victoria 3 building icon, square, with the existing rounded brass frame.
Input images: Image 1 is the exact current cement works icon and EDIT TARGET. Image 2 is supporting insert reference: use ONLY its right-hand cement sack and grey cement powder, not its left limestone blocks.
Primary request: replace the large foreground metal pouring vessel, wheel and stream of molten metal at the lower right of Image 1 with an open burlap sack of grey cement and a small pile of cement powder, matching Image 2's cement. Make cement the clear foreground commodity.
Invariants: preserve the recognizable factory interior behind it, brick furnace, overhead channels, original perspective, warm muted painterly palette and original rounded metallic frame. Do not redesign the building as an outdoor factory. Preserve the composition outside the edited foreground area. Match lighting, grain and scale to the small painted original rather than attaching a photoreal cutout.
Constraints: genuine alpha ONLY outside the rounded frame, opaque scene inside it; no black outer square; no molten metal left in the foreground, no labels, no typography, no watermark. Single finished icon, not a comparison or sheet.

entries.label: Infanterie à mousquet
entries.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: square opaque military-unit illustration for the Victoria 3 mod 1776, PREVIEW revision of the musket infantry.
Input image 1: EDIT TARGET. Preserve the three men's faces, positions, muskets, loading/aiming actions, original camera framing, pale smoky sky, grassy ground and subdued oil-painted brushwork.
Primary request: move the clothing of ALL THREE musketeers about fifty years earlier, to an early-eighteenth-century European infantry look circa 1720–1730. They must look visibly older in uniform design than the later line-infantry type. This is a generic visual evocation, not a named regiment.
Uniform changes: replace the short-looking blue coats and crossed bright white chest straps with long, roomy grey-beige wool justaucorps, broad straight hanging skirts down toward the knees, large low flap pockets, a long row of small simple pewter buttons, very broad deep folded-back muted dark-blue cuffs and NO broad lapels or stiff standing collar. Show a long plain waistcoat underneath, loose knee-breeches where visible, plain linen shirt and simple neckcloth. Use one modest dark brown leather shoulder belt and a waist belt with a worn cartridge pouch, rather than the bold white X of later line infantry. Ordinary unadorned broad-brimmed felt hats cocked in a loose early tricorn shape, no metal badges, feathers, cockades or braid. Worn wool and leather, coherent early cut with small differences in wear between soldiers, not ragged civilian bandits.
Make the older silhouette clearly legible: long untucked coat skirts, broad cuffs, plain unlapelled chest, dark simple straps. Keep the scene's muted earthy palette, painterly realism and the same human identities.
Invariants: exactly the same three main soldiers and actions; preserve the long wooden flintlock muskets and plausible loading hands. No added figures or props. Do not change this into medieval soldiers or seventeenth-century armor; no breastplates, swords raised, pikes or matchlock rests. No late-eighteenth-century fitted coatees, white crossed bandoliers, turned-back white tails, high collars, nineteenth-century shakos, modern firearms or equipment. No border, caption, emblem, lettering or watermark. Full square opaque scene.

entries.label: Bombarde V2 — Europe / repli
entries.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: one square opaque military-unit illustration for Victoria 3 mod 1776, corrected bombard V2.
Input image 1: EDIT TARGET. Preserve the two European attendants, plain early-modern clothes, stone earthwork, a few stone round shot, pale hazy countryside, muted bronze/brown palette and oil-painted brushwork. Change the bombard and its timber bed enough to correct its impossible perspective.
Primary request: rebuild the short heavy bombard as ONE coherent solid tube viewed almost in SIDE PROFILE. Its longitudinal axis runs clearly from LEFT (closed rear/breech) to RIGHT (open muzzle), only slightly angled away into the distance. Camera is nearly perpendicular to this axis, slightly on the muzzle side, NOT a head-on or extreme diagonal view.
Physical geometry: the left end is a clearly CLOSED rounded metal breech. We see its curved side contour, not a second hollow opening or a large rear-facing circular disc. The right end is the ONLY opening, a thick rim around ONE narrow elliptical dark bore. The rim and the reinforcing hoops obey the SAME consistent perspective and axis. Near and far barrel edges stay coherent along the whole length. No twisted or bent barrel, no two mouths, no rear end that appears pointed at the viewer. Make the closed rear and open front unambiguous even at icon size.
Mount: the thick, short, old bronze/iron barrel rests stably on a simple LOW stationary timber cradle with stout longitudinal beams and two supports/wedges. Keep the support geometry tidy and plausible. No tall wheels, no field-gun carriage. Cannon remains the large foreground focal point; both men work on its rear/near side with tools safely away from the muzzle.
Remove the huge firing flash so it cannot conceal or confuse the muzzle. Keep only light drifting powder smoke behind and above it. No flames coming from the breech. Keep the weapon fully inside the square with margins.
Invariants: same two people and painted finish; same old stationary bombard tier, not a modern cannon. No added soldiers, weapons, text, symbols, flags, borders or watermark. Opaque painted sky and ground, ONE completed scene, no diagram, labels, arrows or comparison.

entries.label: Canon de campagne
entries.prompt:
Use case: historical-scene.
Asset type: one square full-canvas opaque military unit illustration for Victoria 3 mod 1776; recognizable at 80 pixels.
Input image 1 is ONLY a painted style and composition reference sheet: match its restrained oil-painted realism, soft brushwork, muted earth colors, light outdoor haze, strong readable foreground silhouette and secondary soldiers. Do not copy the sheet layout, text, modern shakos or uniforms.
Constraints: one cohesive scene only, no border or labels, no flags or insignia, no watermark, no modern equipment. Historical European visual fallback, not asserted to represent all cultures. Primary subject: a mobile eighteenth-century field cannon circa 1776, long bronze barrel mounted on a wooden carriage with TWO tall wooden-spoked wheels and a long trailing timber pointing behind it. Two trained gunners in restrained wool uniforms and black tricorns work the gun on grassy open terrain: one holds a wooden rammer safely clear of the muzzle, another stands beside the wheel. Cannon is the large foreground focal point, three-quarter view, subtle drifting powder smoke. Readable mobile silhouette in contrast to a low stationary bombard. No recoil cylinders, gun shield, rubber tyres, modern breech mechanism, metal turret or nineteenth-century tall shako.
